topic: Claims boundaries in security marketing: what a product's campaign surfaces may say versus what its threat model actually bounds, and how to keep public claims inside the verified envelope

subtopics.scope: The core discipline: a product may publicly claim only what its threat model can bound and its architecture can evidence, nothing stronger.
seed_queries: security product marketing claims must match threat model bounds
security claims versus actual security guarantees threat model

subtopics.scope: Absolute and inflated security language (unhackable, secure by default, impenetrable) and why it collapses under scrutiny.
seed_queries: secure by default misleading security claim examples

subtopics.scope: Regulator and standards guidance on substantiating security claims: FTC enforcement, NIST and EU expectations for evidence behind public statements.
seed_queries: FTC security claims substantiation enforcement cases
NIST guidance truthful vendor security claims evidence

subtopics.scope: Threat models as the bounding document: scope, assumptions, out-of-scope exclusions, and how an assurance case maps public claims to evidence.
seed_queries: threat model document scope assumptions out of scope
security assurance case mapping claims to evidence

subtopics.scope: The verified envelope itself: architecture docs, measured boot and signed trust chains, certifications and attestations that bound what can be claimed.
seed_queries: security architecture documentation supporting product claims
common criteria certification versus vendor marketing claims

subtopics.scope: Maturity and status labeling: technical preview, groundwork, beta versus production support language in READMEs and SECURITY.md supported-versions tables.
seed_queries: technical preview software status README security support

subtopics.scope: How open-source security projects phrase campaign surfaces: taglines, launch pages, README claims for secure boot, immutable OS and identity-root stories.
seed_queries: open source secure boot immutable OS project marketing claims
linux security project launch messaging tagline

subtopics.scope: Operationalizing the boundary: a pre-publication claim review process mapping each marketing claim to a bounded control or evidence artifact.
seed_queries: security marketing claims review checklist process
marketing claim substantiation review security documentation
